raw_output: The patient was admitted for seizures and intracranial hemorrhage. He presented with generalized seizures complicated by tongue biting and hematoma. Head CT revealed left-sided intraparenchymal and subarachnoid hemorrhage. Neurological examination showed right lower facial droop, tongue midline, and weakness in lower extremities. The patient was intubated to assist breathing. After anticoagulation was stopped, he experienced a stroke. He will require rehabilitation at a rehab facility to improve strength and skills. He should follow up with neurologists and vascular surgeons as directed and return to the ED immediately for any new neurological symptoms.

raw_output: The patient was found unresponsive without a pulse and not breathing outside the hospital. EMS performed CPR and successfully restarted the heart. Lab work and EKG revealed a large heart attack. A cardiac cath was performed with stent placement to restore blood flow. Cooling of the body was used to preserve brain function during cardiac arrest. The patient was also not breathing when found. A tube was inserted in the lungs and the patient was ventilated in the ICU. Rib fractures and a pneumothorax occurred due to CPR. A chest tube was placed to allow air to escape the chest. Aspiration pneumonia developed while on the ventilator. Antibiotics were administered, and respiratory status improved. The patient was in the ICU under sedation for a long time while lungs recovered. The patient is now ready for discharge but will experience weakness and fatigue for several months, improving with physical therapy. Medications were adjusted, including metoprolol, atorvastatin, aspirin, and Plavix. Follow-up appointments are required.

It is believed the chronic condition predated her hospitalization, and the acute inflammation was likely caused by a viral infection during the current hospitalization. Both conditions are treated with steroids, and she improved with this treatment. She was discharged on steroids and will follow up with pulmonologists.

He was transferred to the CVICU after the surgery, intubated and sedated, and tolerated the procedure well. He awoke neurologically intact, requiring Precedex for extubation. Postoperative confusion and agitation were treated with Haldol and Zyprexa, and narcotics were discontinued. His mental status improved, and he was extubated on POD#1. He remained in the CVICU until his mental status improved. He was transferred to the step-down unit on POD#7. His mental status returned to baseline, and he was cleared for discharge on POD#9.
